There is, for the same reasons that people use screen or tmux (which some people do use for this).  If I were queueing a prompt I expected to take hours to finish, it would be nice to be able to run it another computer so I don't have to worry about closing my laptop lid or the battery dying.

It's not world-changing, but I have had agents do `grep -r /` commands before and it would have been nice to be able to detach and let it run rather than having to kill it because I have to leave before it'll actually finish (WSL is sooo slow on that).  It would be better if the agent did a better grep, but sometimes I'd rather wait 20 minutes than spend 7 minutes setting it all back up again.

- One of the Chinese LLMs (forget which) has on occasion shown thinking traces where it simulates calling and running a subagent.

- There are some people who believe the models being evaluated during the HF incident were trained to collaborate. It's a very natural next step to produce more effective agentic teams.

next word -> chat -> CoT -> tools -> agentic -> teams

I'm not talking about pumped hydro.  Batteries have largely rendered that obsolete.  And batteries are scaling like gangbusters.

Realize that even in a fully nuclear powered world, huge amounts of batteries are needed.  Replacing every ground vehicle in the US with a 70 kWh BEV would require enough batteries to store about 40 hours of the current average US grid power.  So the scaling is needed regardless of the post-fossil energy source.

A longer term storage mode is also needed to deal with seasonal storage and covering rare Dunkelflauten as batteries are not suitable for that.  Fortunately there are multiple ways that could be handled, so it's a question of which is best.

It always astounds me how unconfigurable most editors are.
